You are an agent who can operate an Android phone on behalf of a user. Based on user's goal/request, you may
- Answer back if the request/goal is a question (or a chat message), like user asks "What is my schedule for today?".
- Complete some tasks described in the requests/goals by performing actions (step by step) on the phone.

When given a user request, you will try to complete it step by step. At each step, a list of descriptions for most UI elements on the current screen will be given to you (each element can be specified by an index), together with a history of what you have done in previous steps. Based on these pieces of information and the goal, you must choose to perform one of the action in the following list (action description followed by the JSON format) by outputing the action in the correct JSON format.
- If you think the task has been completed, finish the task by using the status action with complete as goal_status: `{"action_type": "status", "goal_status": "complete"}`
- If you think the task is not feasible (including cases like you don't have enough information or can not perform some necessary actions), finish by using the `status` action with infeasible as goal_status: `{"action_type": "status", "goal_status": "infeasible"}`
- Answer user's question: `{"action_type": "answer", "text": "<answer_text>"}`
- Click/tap on a UI element (specified by its index) on the screen: `{"action_type": "click", "index": <target_index>}`.
- Long press on a UI element (specified by its index) on the screen: `{"action_type": "long_press", "index": <target_index>}`.
- Type text into an editable text field (specified by its index), this action contains clicking the text field, typing in the text and pressing the enter, so no need to click on the target field to start: `{"action_type": "input_text", "text": <text_input>, "index": <target_index>}`
- Press the Enter key: `{"action_type": "keyboard_enter"}`
- Navigate to the home screen: `{"action_type": "navigate_home"}`
- Navigate back: `{"action_type": "navigate_back"}`
- Scroll the screen or a scrollable UI element in one of the four directions, use the same numeric index as above if you want to scroll a specific UI element, leave it empty when scroll the whole screen: `{"action_type": "scroll", "direction": <up, down, left, right>, "index": <optional_target_index>}`
- Open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed): `{"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": <name>}`
- Wait for the screen to update: `{"action_type": "wait"}`

The current user goal/request is: Delete all but one of any recipes in the Broccoli app that are exact duplicates, ensuring at least one instance of each unique recipe remains

Here is a history of what you have done so far:
Step 1: Action selected: {"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": "Broccoli"}. Opened Broccoli app successfully; now on Recipes list showing multiple recipes, including apparent duplicates like Avocado Toast with Egg (two entries with identical title and description).
Step 2: Action selected: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "down", "index": 4}. Scrolled down the recipe list; more recipes revealed, including two "Eggplant Parmesan" entries (likely non-duplicates due to different descriptions). Continued scrolling is needed to check all items for exact duplicates.
Step 3: Action selected: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "up", "index": 4}. Scrolled up on the recipe list to view earlier items. Now "Avocado Toast with Egg" appears three times (with possibly differing descriptions), and "Baked Cod with Lemon and Dill", "Chicken Caesar Salad Wrap", "Chickpea Vegetable Soup" are also visible. Need to identify exact duplicates among these and delete all but one per unique recipe.
Step 4: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 8}. Clicked on the first "Avocado Toast with Egg" recipe (description: "A delicious and healthy choice...") to open its detail view and look for a delete option. The detail page opened as expected.
Step 5: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 6}. Opened the overflow menu on the Avocado Toast with Egg recipe detail page, revealing Delete, Edit, Share, and Share as file options.
Step 6: Action selected: {"action_type": "navigate_back"}. Closed the overflow menu by navigating back, returning to the recipe detail view; next step is to go back to the recipe list to compare duplicates.
Step 7: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 4}. Navigated back from recipe detail to the main list, where multiple "Avocado Toast with Egg" duplicates are now visible along with other recipes.
Step 8: Action selected: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "down", "index": 4}. Scrolled down the recipe list to reveal more recipes; now visible are Chickpea Vegetable Soup, two Eggplant Parmesan entries, Garlic Butter Shrimp, Lemon Garlic Tilapia, and Moroccan Chickpea Stew, indicating duplicates exist further down.
Step 9: Action selected: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "up", "index": 4}. Scrolled up on the recipe list to reveal previously hidden items at the top; now visible are three "Avocado Toast with Egg" duplicates, along with other unique recipes, enabling duplicate detection.
Step 10: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 12}. Opened the second "Avocado Toast with Egg" duplicate (identical title and description) to access its details and eventually delete it. Successfully navigated to the recipe detail view.
Step 11: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 6}. Tapped the "More options" button on the duplicate "Avocado Toast with Egg" recipe detail page, which successfully opened a popup menu containing "Delete" (among Share, Share as file, Edit). Next step: select "Delete" to remove this duplicate.
Step 12: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 3}. We need to summarize the step based on the action and the before/after screenshots. The action was clicking on "Delete" (index 3) in the popup menu. The before screenshot shows a popup with options: Share, Share as file, Edit, Delete. The after screenshot shows a confirmation dialog: "Delete this recipe?" with CANCEL
Step 13: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 2}. Confirmed deletion of a duplicate recipe by tapping 'DELETE' on the confirmation dialog; returned to the main recipes list where the duplicate is now removed.
Step 14: Action selected: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "down", "index": 4}. Scrolled down the recipe list; revealed new items including duplicate "Eggplant Parmesan" (two entries with different descriptions), plus Garlic Butter Shrimp, Lemon Garlic Tilapia, Moroccan Chickpea Stew, and Pesto Pasta with Peas. Exact duplicates require matching title and description, so further inspection is needed.
Step 15: Action selected: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "up", "index": 4}. Scrolled up to the top of the recipe list; revealed two Avocado Toast with Egg entries with different descriptions (not exact duplicates), and other unique recipes.
Step 16: Action selected: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "down", "index": 4}. Scrolled down the recipe list; revealed new items including two 'Eggplant Parmesan' entries with different descriptions (not exact duplicates), plus other recipes. Need to continue scrolling and compare full title/description/source to find exact duplicates.
Step 17: Action selected: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "up", "index": 4}. Scrolled up the recipe list to reveal the top, now seeing two "Avocado Toast with Egg" entries (potential duplicates) and other recipes; worked as intended.
Step 18: Action selected: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "down", "index": 4}. Scrolled down the recipe list; revealed more items (Eggplant Parmesan appears twice but with different descriptions, so not exact duplicates). Need to continue scrolling to inspect all recipes for exact duplicates.
Step 19: Action selected: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "down", "index": 4}. Scrolled down the recipe list; now visible are three identical Shrimp Avocado Salad entries (exact duplicates) and two Quinoa Salad entries with different descriptions (not duplicates). Next, need to delete two of the Shrimp Avocado Salad duplicates.
Step 20: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 27}. Clicked on the second duplicate "Shrimp Avocado Salad" (index 27) to open its detail page; successfully navigated to the recipe detail view, where deletion can be performed. There are three identical Shrimp Avocado Salad recipes; this step aims to delete one duplicate.
Step 21: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 6}. Clicked the "More options" (three-dot menu) on the "Shrimp Avocado Salad" recipe detail page to open the overflow menu, which now reveals Share, Edit, and Delete options — next step: select Delete to remove this duplicate.
Step 22: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 3}. Clicked "Delete" on the overflow menu for a duplicate recipe, which opened a confirmation dialog ("Delete this recipe?") with CANCEL and DELETE buttons. Ready to confirm deletion.
Step 23: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 2}. Confirmed deletion of a duplicate 'Shrimp Avocado Salad' recipe; returned to the recipes list, where additional duplicates of that recipe still remain.
Step 24: Action selected: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "down", "index": 4}. Scrolled down to reveal the third Shrimp Avocado Salad's description as "An ideal recipe..." matching the first, confirming it's a duplicate.
